        Myron and Carrie Hafner family

Myron and Carrie Hafner

Myron Herbert Hafner, born Jan. 15, 1939, grew up on his grandparents' homestead
north of Beulah. He attended Kronthal Elementary School and was confirmed at
Kronthal Trinity Lutheran Church. Growing up he was active in the Riverside 4-H
Club and was on the livestock judging team.

Many changes occurred in the area during this time. Due to the construction of
the Garrison Dam, the Missouri River, just north of their farm, changed from a
lazy river that flooded sub-irrigated alfalfa to a large lake that enhances
recreation, allows irrigation, controls flooding and generates electrical
power. Myron's father and uncles set up a sawmill in their yard to utilize the
large beautiful trees along the river banks before the trees succumbed to the
back-up water from the dam.

While attending Beulah High School, Myron was a member of FFA and on the
livestock judging team. He graduated from Beulah High School in 1956. After a
year of helping his father on the farm, he served in the Marine Corps for three
years.

On Aug. 20, 1960, Myron married Caroline (Carrie) Lee Wolf, daughter of Herbert
and Lydia Wolf. Myron and Carrie farm north of Beulah and are partners in Lake
Shore Estates.

The Hafners have two children. Robyn Lynn is married to Gaylen Skalsky and they
have three children, Brandon Lee (Aug. 27, 1981), Joslyn Marie (April 21, 1983)
and Kyle Micheal (July 19, 1987) . Rance Jay Hafner is married to Joan
Kruckenberg and they have two girls; Brooke Elizabeth (June 16, 1981) and Tessa
Rochelle (Sept. 1, 1985).

"Many changes occurred during our lifetime. School changed from many rural
schools to several large schools in the city of Beulah. The city itself has
grown by leaps and bounds and is no longer a small town where everyone knows
everybody else. We enjoy the progress but also miss some of the old times,"
they write.

Myron is the oldest son of Herbert Jacob Hafner (May 15, 1913-Aug. 25, 1969) and
Katherine (Oberlander) Hafner (Sept. 4, 1914). They farmed Herbert's parents'
homestead until Herb's death in 1969. Katie continued to live on the farm until
1974 when she moved into Beulah. She is a member of Concordia Lutheran Church,
Concordia Lutheran Women's Missionary League and has been in charge of quilting
for World Relief for many years. Katie is also a member of the Nursing Home
Auxiliary and is active in Senior Citizens.

Herb and Katie had four children:

Myron married to Carrie, they have two children; Adella (March 10, 1941)
married to Darold Benz, they have three children; Herman (Sept. 12, 1944) has
two sons, Spencer Herbert (March 24, 1971) and Patrick Dale (April 16, 1972).
Herman married Elizabeth Waln Jan. 15, 1982; she has one son, Shad Russell Waln
(June 30, 1971); and David (Sam) (Sept. 28, 1946), who lives on the family farm.

Carrie attended school in Beulah where she was a cheerleader, active in 4-H and
FHA and a school librarian. She graduated in 1960.

Through the years the Hafners have been very active in the community. They
received the North Dakota Outstanding Young Farmer Award in 1971.

Myron is a member of the Beulah school board and has served as chairman for many
years. He served on the Mercer County planning and zoning board and as a
director of the Beulah Farmers Union Oil Station Board for six years.

Myron was a charter member of the Beulah Jaycees and held several offices,
including local president and state treasurer. He received the JCI Senator
Award.

Carrie was active in Mrs. Jaycees and was named First Year Outstanding Jaycee
and Outstanding Mrs. Jaycee on both the local and state level. She held many
local offices and served as state director, secretary and was state president
in 1973-74.

Carrie was awarded the Jaycee Distinguished Service Award and the Keywoman
Award in 1977, and was named to Outstanding Young Women of America. She served
as chairman of the Mercer County Task Force Human Resource committee, was a 4-H
leader for 20 years and is presently vice president of the Mercer County Fair
Board.

The Hafners are members of Concordia Lutheran Church. Myron has served as
Sunday school superintendent, was on the building committee and is an elder.
Carrie is a member of the Lutheran Women's Missionary League and has held the
offices of guild vice president, president, executive board president and zone
president.

Carrie is employed as a secretary and enjoys knitting and sewing.

        Patty Hamby     Tyrone Hamby

        Grady and Lillian Hamby

Grady and Lillian Hamby

Grady Hamby was born Aug. 15, 1921, the second oldest of six brothers, in
Tennessee, to Alger and Callie Hamby. During World War II he worked as a welder
in the Norfolk Naval Shipyard.

Grady first came to Beulah in 1948 where he worked on an addition to the Beulah
Power Plant. He met and married Lillian Menge in 1949. Lillian was born in Hazen
on April 29, 1934, the youngest of 12 children born to John and Elizabeth Menge.
She grew up on a farm north of Hazen and attended school in Beulah. They have
two children, Tyrone, born on July 10, 1950, and Patricia, in 1953.

Working construction as a pipefitter-welder required the family to move
frequently around the country, living in North Carolina, Tennessee, Ohio and
South Dakota. The government installation of missiles in North Dakota brought
the family back to the state in 1961. A good construction environment allowed
the family to remain in Beulah through to the present. In addition to the
missile fields around Minot, Grady worked on the Stanton and Center power
plants, the ABM site, the Underwood power plants, the Beulah power plants, and
the gasification plant at Beulah before retiring in 1986. Lillian currently
works at Sakakawea Medical Center in Hazen. The family are members of Zion
Lutheran Church.

Patricia graduated from Beulah High School in 1971, married Archie Ludwig of

currently lives in Minneapolis, Minn.

Tyrone graduated from Beulah High School in 1968 and from NDSU in 1972. He
married Shirley Younker of Beulah and has two children, Marcus and Derek. Tyrone
is now single and is a Major (P) in the U.S. Army stationed at U.S. Space
Command in Colorado Springs.

Herman and Vivian Hauff

Herman Hauff was born on a farm in rural Golden Valley, N.D. on May 22, 1914.
Both of his parents are deceased, Gottlieb in September 1939 and Mary (Berg) in
September 1962. Herman's wife is Vivian (Scheidt), born April 10, 1927, south of
Beulah. Vivian's father, John, passed away Jan. 16, 1965, and her mother,
Gladys, is living in Beulah. The Hauffs have four children, Joanne, born June
2, 1949, Bismarck; Jerry, born April 27, 1953, Hazen; Mary Ann, born Feb. 8,
1958, Hazen; and Janice, born July 12, 1959, Hazen.

Herman is the son of German Rumanian immigrants who started farming here in
1907, near Golden Valley. Herman and Vivian were married Sept. 5, 1946, and
lived north of Golden Valley until they moved to Beulah in 1950. Back in the
'40s it was considered a privilege for farm children to attend high school and
everyone had to sacrifice something in the family to get a good education.
Students usually stayed with relatives or rented sleeping rooms with light
housekeeping facilities. The Hauffs' move to Beulah was primarily accomplished
because of the excellent school system here in the county.

While attending school, Vivian had the good fortune to have a very dedicated
teacher, Joan Boland, for four of the eight years. The school was a one-room
building in the country near her parents' home. Vivian worked for Carl
Thelander and Albert Wolf in the RCU grocery and clothing store during her
junior and senior years of high school. Vivian graduated from Beulah High
School in 1945 and then attended Dickinson State College for a period of time
after which she taught rural school for three years, one year in Beulah and two
in the Golden Valley area.

The Hauffs purchased the Gambles Store at 116 E. Main, Beulah, in December of
1950 and managed it until retirement in 1979.

Herman and Vivian are very thankful for the way the Lord has blessed and
protected their family through the years and the following is some history of
their children.

Joanne was active in 4-H during grade and high school and graduated from Beulah
High School and then attended Dickinson State College, majoring in elementary
education, and received her bachelor of science degree in 1971. Joanne married
Gregory Haugland, son of Goodwin and Marlys Haugland of Crosby, N.D. on Dec.
28, 1970. The couple taught school in South Heart, N.D. before moving to
Beulah. Joanne currently teaches the sixth grade, and Greg is the high school
principal.

Jerry was active in Boy Scouts and athletics and played center on the Miner
basketball team which represented Beulah at the state tournament in 1971. He
attended North Dakota State University, majoring in agriculture education, and
received his bachelor of science degree in 1975 and his master of science
degree in agriculture economics in 1981. Jerry taught school at Killdeer and
UND Williston Branch, and works at the present time as a commercial credit
officer for the Farm Credit Services of Mandan. Jerry married Denise Teske,
daughter of Bernard and Mae Teske of Hazen, on June 15, 1985. Denise is a
commercial art teacher for the Bismarck schools. Denise and Jerry have one
child, Logan.

Mary Ann was active in 4-H, played girls' basketball and worked as a swimming
pool lifeguard. She graduated from Beulah High School in 1976, attended North
Dakota State University and received her bachelor of science degree in 1981.
Mary Ann married Glenn Randy Prigge, June 20, 1981, son of Glenn and Lila
Prigge of Grand Forks. She is employed by the school for the blind in Grand
Forks. Randy is engaged in farming north of Grand Forks, and they have two
daughters, Amber and Kayla.

Janice was also active in 4-H, played girls' basketball and worked as a
swimming pool lifeguard. She graduated from Beulah High School in 1977,
attended NDSU and graduated from the Bismarck Hospital School of Nursing in
1984 as a registered nurse. She is currently employed by the medical center in
Bismarck. Janice married Michael Merkel, son of Kenneth and Verna Merkel of
Mandan, on April 20, 1979. Michael is employed at the Fallkirk Mining Co.

Greg and Joanne Haugland

Greg Haugland was born Aug. 31, 1949, in Crosby, N.D., to Goodwin and Marlys
Haugland. The elder Hauglands still reside in Crosby.

Joanne is the daughter of Herman and Vivian Hauff of Beulah. She was born June
2, 1949, in Bismarck, but she grew up in Beulah. Joanne and Greg were married on
Dec. 27, 1970.

Greg writes, "After teaching in South Heart, N.D., our family moved to Beulah
where I was named basketball coach and high school principal. Joanne teaches
sixth grade."

They have now been in Beulah in their present positions for 13 years. Since
Joanne is originally from Beulah, and left for a number of years before
returning permanently, she has seen some changes. The most noticeable changes,
for her, have occurred in the school system which, as a teacher, she knows well.

Joanne says, "The size of the system has grown, quite obviously, but so have the
educational choices and experiences available to the students. There are many
more opportunities here now for students than there were for me. There are also
many more students."

Joanne went to school in the "old school" (now the middle school) and, as a
sophomore, moved out to the "boonies" where the new building was located. This
location could adequately be described as being in the middle of a lot of
fields - just a big school and considerable prairie.

After she had gone off to college, married, and lived away for a while, the
changed Beulah she returned to felt very positive. For one thing, everything
had boomed - and the high school now sat in the middle of a new subdivision.
"But," says Joanne, "the really pleasant thing is that the school system only
kept pace with the growth. It wasn't overbuilt. And, even with the problems
associated with rapid population growth, the influx of new ideas and points of
view coming in with the outsiders has only helped Beulah become a more
interesting place to live.

The Hauglands have two children, Tami, born March 24, 1974, and Kari, born Oct.
29, 1976, both in Bismarck.

Greg and Joanne are members of Zion Lutheran Church, the Beulah Quarterback
Club, the Eagles Club, and the Beulah Chamber of Commerce.

Frederick and Betty Hausauer

On March 28, 1935, Frederick Hausauer was born to Phillip and Christina. Fred's
father Phillip passed away Feb. 27, 1961, and his mother Christina (Flemmer) is
still living. Fred married Betty Mae (Tesky), and she was born May 12, 1941, in
Beulah. Betty's parents, John and Lydia (Guthmiller), are both with the Lord.
John Tesky passed away April 21, 1967, and Lydia passed away May 24, 1984.

Fred was born and raised on his parents' farm between Beulah and Glen Ullin. He
attended rural school and the rural Peace Lutheran Church. He served in the
Armed Forces from April 1957 until March of 1959 and was stationed in Germany
for 18 months.

Betty was raised on her parents' farm eight miles north of Beulah and attended

married April 12, 1959, and lived on her parents' farm until November 1959. They
moved into Beulah where they lived until March 7, 1987, and then moved to a farm
four miles north of Zap. Fred has been employed at the Knife River Coal Mine
since October, 1959. They attend the Beulah Church of God. Fred and Betty have

Rae. Marilyn and James live four miles north of Zap.

Eugene attended Beulah schools and married Dara Zeiszler, July 11, 1987. Eugene
is employed by Galster Grain Farms. Eugene and Dara live nine miles north of
Zap.

Fred and Betty remember when the Dreamland Pavilion and Roxy Theater were the
center of social activities in Beulah, when the stores were open on Saturday
night and all the farmers came to town.

Peter and Emelia Hausauer

Peter's father Jacob Hausauer Sr. was born in Glueckstahl, South Russia on
March 26, 1874 and his wife Marie (Treftz) Hausauer was born in Glueckstahl,
South Russia on Feb. 11, 1878. Jacob Sr. and his wife were baptized, confirmed,
and married in the same church. They were united in marriage in 1898.

Jacob and his family came to the United States on May 20, 1906 and lived in
Jamestown, ND for three years where Jacob was employed with the Northern Pacific
Railroad. On Oct. 9, 1909 they came to Hebron, ND by immigrant rail car. The
Hausauers put most of their belongings into storage at the Hebron Lumber Yard
and, with their team and wagon, started on a two-day trip to the Dan Lapp
homestead 27 miles northwest of Hebron. During the winter of 1909 Jacob built a
house on his own homestead located 12 miles southwest of Golden Valley in
S.6-T.142-R.90, near the Dunn County line. In 1917 Jacob purchased an
additional quarter of land adjoining the homestead and in 1929 another quarter
of land was added.

The family had four children which had all been born in Russia when they
settled in Mercer County. They were Jacob (Jack) Jr., born May 1, 1898, Rose,
June 20, 1901, Katherin, June 6, 1903, and Christina, May 22, 1905. Two
additional children were born on the homestead southwest of Golden Valley. They
were Peter, Sept. 4, 1910 and Emma, Aug. 11, 1914.

Pete and Emelia Hausauer

Jacob Sr. and Marie lived on the homestead until Oct. 6, 1936, when they moved
to Hebron and Peter took over the farm. Jacob Sr. passed away on April 5, 1951
and Marie passed away on May 12, 1952.

Peter attended public school at the Walker school district south of Golden
Valley. He was confirmed on March 28, 1926 in the Golgotha Lutheran Church at
Golden Valley by Pastor E.H. Vetter. Pete was married to Emelia Keierleber on
Dec . 5, 1933 at Hebron. Emilia (Keierleber) Hausauer, daughter of Henry and
Elizabeth (Sauter) Keierleber, was born on May 3, 1914 at Hebron. Emelia was
the third of seven children and was baptized on Sept. 17, 1914 in St. John's
Lutheran Church at Hebron with Peter and Magdalena Roth as sponsors. Emelia
attended public school in Hebron. Her parents, Henry and Elizabeth Keierleber,
immigrated to the United States from Johonastal, South Russia in 1910. Four
children were born to Pete and Emelia Hausauer: Marion (Mrs. Otto Rasch),
Violet (deceased, Mrs. Duane Pletan), Ruth (Mrs. Roger Smith), and Stanley.

They also have 11 grandchildren and six great-grandchildren. Pete and Emelia
celebrated their 55th Anniversary on Dec. 5, 1988.

Pete has many memories of his younger days. Going to school with a one-horse
buggy when its was 20 below and eating frozen lunches. The teacher would walk to
school most of the time and get the fire started and the kids would all sit
around the coal stove until dinner time. Sometimes the teacher would even send
them outside so they could play and exercise to get warm.

Much of the social activity of the families were the Basket Socials, dances and
skits put on by the children. The school would be packed even on the coldest
nights.

His parents had a lot a hardships back in those days, and also a lot of
courage. Food was not plentiful and they all had to do a lot of hard work to
survive. They dug their own coal and had to haul water from a considerable
distance. "I remember when my dad bought a quarter of land joining the
homestead that was all grassland. He broke it up with a one-bottom breaking
plow pulled by five horses," Pete recalls. "There were a lot of rocks and it
was back-breaking work to clear the land. I used to carry lunch to Dad in the
morning and afternoon. It was fun for me to run after the gophers and pick up
some of the smaller rocks. I still have that one-bottom plow on my lot in
Halliday.

"There was one prairie fire that I remember very well. It started northwest of
the homestead and there was a strong west wind. People came from all directions
with wagons and barrels of water. The cattle, horses and wild animals were
running in front of the fire and you could see that some of the cattle and
rabbits had been burned. As the fire came closer my mother and another lady put
us kids in a wagon and started for the sod house. Some more help came and
started a back fire around the house. I don't recall just how far the fire
spread but I know it went a long distance to the east. This occurred in about
1915 or 1916.

"There used to be wild horses that roamed the country and at times there were as
many as 150 to 200 horses in a bunch. If you had any hay stacks out that were
not fenced or grain that was not threshed someone would have to stand guard at
night. I remember a lot of young cowboys that used to come looking for jobs and
they would be carrying a pistol and a 30-30 rifle.

"This was real exciting for me and the boys would give me a ride on their
horses, which I really enjoyed. I continued to keep my love for horses that I
developed as a child and when we moved to Werner, ND on July 3, 1945 I
continued to raise horses and cattle. Our home two and one-half miles west of
Werner (S22-T145-R93) gave us better grazing land with lots of accessible water
and also provided a good school system for our children," Pete said.

Pete and Emelia continued to farm, raise cattle and horses until their
retirement in October, 1978, when they moved to Halliday.

"We are very thankful that our parents had the opportunity to come to the United
States and that we were raised here where everyone has a chance to work and
worship as they believe," Pete said.

"We are thankful, as we grow older, that God and this country have given us many
golden opportunities."

Phillip and Christina (Flemmer) Hausauer

Phillip P. Hausauer was born Feb. 10, 1896, in South Russia to Phillip and
Rosina (Huber) Hausauer. He came to America with his parents in 1905. His
father died Feb. 16, 1960, and his mother on Nov. 1, 1932. Phillip was married
Dec. 31, 1918, at the county church where he had met his bride, Christina
Flemmer, who was born Aug. 30, 1900, at Glueckstahl, Odessa, Russia to Jacob
and Fredericka (Jacober) Flemmer.

Christina came to America with her parents in the spring of 1906. She and her
father were the only ones in her family who didn't get seasick on the trip to
America. Phillip and Christina were both raised on farms located between Beulah
and Glen Ullin, ND. After their marriage they lived on his father's farm. In
1920 Phillip, Jr. took over the farm and his parents moved into Beulah.

The Hausauers were members of the rural Peace Lutheran Church and now Christina
is a member of Zion Lutheran Church. They did most of their business in Glen
Ullin in the early years. Later when Beulah grew and had more businesses they
traveled to Beulah to shop. In the fall of 1956 they sold the farm and moved
into Beulah where Christina continues to live in their home. They raised 15
children who attended the rural school, but the three youngest finished their
education in the Beulah school.

Phillip died Feb. 27, 1961. There are 38 living grandchildren, one deceased, 41
great-grandchildren living, two deceased, and three great-great-grandchildren.

Christina enjoys having her family around. It is a close family and since it is
a large family, they have been renting the Senior Citizen's building for family
gatherings such as her birthday and Christmas.

        Phillip and Rosina Hausauer in their shoe repair shop.

Phillip and Rosina Hausauer

Phillip Hausauer and Rosina Huber were both born and raised in Glueckstahl,
South Russia. He was born on July 16, 1874, and she was born on Sept. 4, 1872.
They were married in Glueckstahl in 1893. In 1905, they immigrated to America.
Phillip and Rosina had two children, one of whom, Phillip Jr. was born Feb. 10,
1896, in South Russia. Daughter Louise was born on Jan. 19, 1906, in rural Glen
Ullin.

For a time, Phillip and Rosina stayed with Phillip's brother, Peter, in Marian,
S.D. Then, in 1906, the year Louise was born, they were able to take up a
homestead 17 miles south of Beulah. In 1920, Phillip turned the farm over to
his son, Phillip Jr., and moved to Beulah, where he purchased a shoe repair
shop. This shop was located about where Benz Insurance stands today. It was
called the Beulah Shoe Shop.

Phillip put the soles on the shoes and Rosina did the sewing. They had living
quarters in the back of the store. They would still go out to the farm and help
their son out at harvest time.

The Hausauers were members of the Peace Lutheran Church between Beulah and Glen
Ullin.

After his wife died in 1932, Phillip quit the shoe repair business. He
continued living in the shop until about 1952 when he became a resident of the
Joachim retirement home where he lived for eight years, until his death. He
passed away at the Hazen hospital Feb. 16, 1960.

His son, Phillip, married Christina Flemmer. They had 15 children. Phillip Jr.
died Feb. 27, 1961. Louise married William Ost and had four children. She died
March 9, 1944. (Betty is married to Fred, son of Phillip Jr.)

Emil and Emma Heihn

Emil Rueben Heihn was born May 6, 1911, at Goodrich, which is in Sheridan
County, to Gottlieb and Katharina (Schlenker) Heihn. His father died Feb. 22,
1951, and his mother died on Feb. 18, 1943. Emil married Emma Rosina Fischer on
Jan. 17, 1937. Emma was born Nov. 18, 1911, near Zap to Abraham and Maria
(Mattheis) Fischer. Her father died Jan. 1, 1953, and her mother on Oct. 11,
1976. Both sets of parents also lived at Beulah.

Emil worked at various jobs around the Beulah area including M.P. Moore, Beulah
mine tipple, garbage collection and reading meters for the city of Beulah, and
also worked on farms and on construction. Some of the jobs Emma held were at the
Joachim Memorial Home, Beulah Nursing Home, housework and child care.

Emma was treasurer of German Ladies Aid of Zion Lutheran Church in 1945,
treasurer of Ladies Guild Homemakers Club in 1948 and treasurer of Volunteer Red
Cross Gray Ladies in 1974. They are parents of one adopted son, Gerald "Sam"
Heihn, born Aug. 7, 1936, at Beulah. He married Patricia Hodgetts of Washington
and they had one daughter, Roberta (Heihn) Gardner, who lives in Seattle,
Wash., with her two children, Matthew and Sarah. Gerald lives at Hesperia,
Calif. Emil Heihn passed away April 3, 1984, at the Bismarck Hospital. Emma
makes her home in Beulah.

Emma writes, "The first year we lived in Beulah, there was a big flood due to a
cloudburst the Fourth of July (1937). It washed the soil out of our garden.
Emil and I along with Mr. and Mrs. Jake Keller and family went in our Model A
Ford to drive away from the flood. Our car got wet and stalled. We floated for
a block before someone threw a rope and we followed it over to dry land. The
water was four feet deep. The water was up to our waist in the car. Mrs. Wagner
and her five small children were in their house when it started to float down
to Main Street. They were all safe since she had put the children up on tables.
There were no electric wires in those days."

        Theodore and Martha Heihn

Ted and Martha Heihn

Ted was born on the family farm, three miles north of Beulah, on Oct. 3, 1903.
His parents were Karl Jr. and Rosina (Geiszler) Heihn.

Before he was married, Ted worked on the road construction gang that built old
Highway 49 and old Highway 25. In those days roads were built using horse-drawn
equipment and manpower. In 1934 he began working for the underground Knife
River Coal Mine as a car spotter. Ted and Martha (Pfenning) Heihn were married
on Aug. 23, 1936, at the Kronthal Lutheran Church with Pastor Schaeffer
officiating. In 1937 Ted had a permanent injury accident at the mine where the
other miner involved was killed. He could not go to work for a year. In 1953
when the underground mine closed, Ted was laid off as were many miners.  At the
time he was working as a machine operator. He went back to doing construction
work and carpentry. Ted has been semi-retired since 1963, but has always kept
busy doing small carpentry jobs and volunteer work.

Ted is a past member of the Progressive Mine Union Local No. 1101 and Zion
Lutheran Brotherhood. He is now a member of the Beulah Eagles, lifetime member
of the Mercer County Historical Society, Beulah Chapter of the Germans from
Russia Historical Society and the Beulah Senior Citizens.

Martha was born on the family farm in the Kronthal area to Amelia (Koehler)
Pfenning and Michael Pfenning on Nov. 5, 1915. Martha worked as a housewife
until 1962 when she became employed at the Beulah Community Nursing Home and in
1965 she was hired as manager of the Joachim Memorial Home. She was employed at
the home until July, 1981, when the home merged with the Beulah Community
Nursing Home.

Martha has been a past member of Zion Lutheran German Ladies Aid, Zion's W.M.F.,
Ladies Guild Homemakers, Royal Neighbors, Beulah Mission Band, Nursing Home
Gray Ladies, Sunday school teacher, 4-H and Girl Scoutleader. She is presently a
lifetime and charter member of the Mercer County Historical Society, on which
she serves on the board of directors, a charter member of the Beulah Eagles
Auxiliary, A.L.C.W., Beulah Senior Citizens, coordinator of the West River
Transportation Council and is associated with the Ombudsman Program at the
Nursing Home.

When Martha retired in 1981, she and Ted started an "on-going" rummage sale in
their home garage. Items were brought and donated to them and they would clean,
sort and sell all the rummage for charity. The total proceeds after three years
were equally divided between the Historical Society and the Nursing Home.

When the Senior Citizens opened their center in the old Joachim Memorial Home,
Ted and Martha moved their rummage sale to the center's basement with the Senior
Citizen Center getting the proceeds. They each donate about 15 hours a week to
this project.

Ted and Martha had three daughters; Janice who was born Nov. 14, 1937 at the
Granum Maternity Home at Beulah, and died at the Hazen Memorial Hospital on
Jan. 13, 1955, of heart failure. She was a senior at Beulah High School at the
time of her death. Caroline was born on April 1, 1939, at the Bismarck
Hospital. She married Sharold Oster of Hazen in 1962. She died of cancer on
March 17, 1975. Mary Lou was born April 27, 1948, at Bismarck Hospital. Mary
Lou married Terry Horning in August 1978. They live in the house that Ted built
all by himself, working from 1945-1949. The Heihns have six grandchildren:
David, Laura, and Mary Jan Oster and Jason, Justin and Brooke Horning.

Harold and Vera Heine

Harold Herbert Heine, son of Mr. and Mrs. Samuel and Lena Heine and Mary
(Unterseher) Heine, was born March 16, 1923, at Zap. They moved from Zap to
Beulah in 1934. Harold was in the CCC from 1939 to 1941. In 1942-43, he worked
for Fred Flemmer in the Ford garage. Sam Heine passed away March 22, 1970, and
Lena Heine passed away June 24, 1978.

On July 24, 1943, at Wibaux, Mont., Harold married Vera Thompson. Vera
(Thompson) Heine was born Dec. 4, 1923, to Manley and Isabell (Henderson)
Thompson of Beulah. Manley Thompson passed away Dec. 6, 1982, and Isabell
passed away Sept. 23, 1985. Vera was born in Beulah and enjoyed growing up in
Beulah because she knew all the kids in school. It was all in an old
schoolhouse and she knew where everyone lived.

        Harold and Vera Heine

A lot of the kids enjoyed going roller skating at the Sheep Shed. There was
sledding in the winter on the Stickney hill and ice skating in town. Vera saved
her allowance for the shows at the Roxy Theatre, where she paid a quarter per
ticket. That was in the 1930s and 1940s.

The Heines then moved to Mandan where Harold worked in the Ford garage. On
Sept. 15, 1944, they came back to Beulah where Harold started working for Knife
River Coal in the underground coal mine. He worked there until April, 1952. From
there, he went to work for Montana-Dakota Utilities and worked there until
April 1983.

Harold has held various offices such as president, secretary, elder, and board
of education member in their church. Vera held office as president of her
homemaker's club, "The Ladies Guild."

Harold and Vera had four daughters: Diane May, born Sept. 22, 1945; Mary Bell,
born Aug. 12, 1948; June Ann, born June 7, 1956; and Lucinda Sue, born July 22,
1964.

        Mary and Larry Bullinger, Kristy and Chad

Clifford and Diana Helm

Clifford Helm was born at Beulah on Sept. 10, 1940, to Jack and Clara (Ellwein)
Helm. He lived in Zap until 1946, then moved to Gascoyne, ND. In 1951 the family
moved back to Beulah.

Diana Helm was born June 27, 1946, at Hazen, to Albert and Regina (Miller)
Knoell. She grew up on a farm north of Hazen.

Clifford and Diana were married at Peace Lutheran Church in Hazen on Oct. 16,
1964. They have two children: Debbie, born Jan. 11, 1966, and Randy, born April
30, 1970. Debbie is married to Faron Scherer and they have a daughter, Tiffany,
born Feb. 7, 1988.

The Helms are members of Concordia Lutheran Church, where Clifford has served
several years as trustee and as a member of the Board of Stewardship. Clifford
served in the U.S. Army, stationed in Germany. He has worked for Knife River
Coal since 1966.

Diana works for Mercer County ASCS. She has served several years as church
secretary and is a member of the LWML, Naomi Guild and the Board of Education.
She has taught Sunday school, Bible school, and confirmation classes. She is
also a member of the Cheerful Homemakers Club and has participated for many
years in league bowling.

The family enjoys summers when they can spend free time boating at Lake
Sakakwea.

Fred and Kathryn Helm

Fred Helm was born and raised south of Dodge, ND, on Feb. 20, 1909 to Ludwig
and Christina (Fisher) Helm. Ludwig and Christina farmed there for many years
until they moved into Zap, where Ludwig ran a butcher shop until he retired.
They raised six sons and two daughters. Ludwig passed away in 1961 and
Christina in 1967.

Fred attended school in the Dodge area and worked on local farms and ranches as
a young boy. He worked as a mechanic in South Dakota and as part of his wages he
was taught how to fly. He received his private pilot's license at the age of
17. This was a lifelong love of Fred's and he used it not only as a hobby, but
also started the Zap Airport in 1941. Fred ran many air shows during which they
would offer rides to customers and put on aerial stunt shows for the customers.
During some of the hard winters, Fred would drop groceries, mail and other
supplies to the stranded country people. He also operated an emergency airlift
to the sick and even picked up corpses.

        Fred Helm family: Janet, Kathryn, Fred, Delano, Carole

Fred flew around the country and would often offer rides to anyone who seemed
interested. This is how Fred met his bride. Fred was married to Kathryn Gienger
on July 7, 1939. He flew across the river many times to court her and finally
they eloped and were married in Mandan, ND.

Kathryn was born on March 24, 1921 to Gustov and Kathryn (Dockter) Gienger.
Gustov and Kathryn were both born in South Russia and came to settle in the
small community of Lincoln Valley, ND. Here they raised four sons and four
daughters. Gustov and Kathryn farmed near Anamoose, ND for many years. Gustov
died in 1945 and Kathryn passed away in 1974.

When Fred and Kathryn were first married they moved to their home in the Zap
strip mine. Fred worked at Dakota Collieries until 1941, when they moved into
Zap and Fred was engaged in farming. In 1952 he started his own construction
company which he operated until his death.

Fred was a member of Pilots Aeronautical Association for 34 years. Kathryn
served on the Mercer County Farm Bureau board, a charter member of the Mercer
County Gray Ladies, Mercer County Civil Defense, Mercer County Historical
Society and for six years was on the Mercer-McLean Library Board. She is also
past chairman of the Beulah Christian Women's Club. She is a member of Immanuel
Baptist Church of Beulah.

Fred and Kathryn resided in Zap for 25 years. They moved to Beulah in 1968,
where Kathryn still resides.

They had three children: Delano (Woody) born in 1949 at Mandan. Woody and his
wife, Lupe, live in Los Angeles, CA. Woody graduated from Jamestown College and
is a manager for K-Mart Stores.

Janet was born in 1941 and is married to Ray Thielman. Janet graduated from
Jamestown College and teaches German and history at Jamestown High School. They
have two daughters.

Carole (Dallman) was born in 1945. Carole attended Dickinson State College and
resides in Beulah. She is presently working for the Chamber of Commerce. Carole
has four children.

Jack and Clara Helm

Jack T. Helm was born June 4, 1916, in a sod house in Dunn County near Dodge.
His parents, Ludwig and Christina Helm, farmed until they moved to Zap in 1937
where Ludwig owned and operated a butcher shop.

        Jack Helm family Noel, Jack, Norbert. Front: Patsy, Clara, Clifford.

Clara Helm was born in Zeeland, SD, on Jan. 15, 1921, to Andrew and Emelia
Ellwein. She lived in Beulah as a young girl, moving to Zap at the age of
seven, where her father worked as janitor at the Zap school.

The Helms lived in Zap until 1946 when they moved to Gascoyne, ND. In 1951 they
moved to Beulah where the Helm brothers (Jack and Emanuel) started a strip
mining operation.  In 1952 they sold it to Knife River Coal Mining Company.
Jack worked at Knife River as general foreman until his retirement in 1979.

Jack was a member of the Beulah City Council for eight years, serving as street
commissioner and police commissioner. He was also a member of the Chamber of
Commerce.

Clara Helm worked at the Beulah Nursing Home for five years. She taught Sunday
school for many years at Concordia Lutheran Church and was a member of the
LWML. She was also active for many years on a bowling league.

Jack and Clara raised four children: Noel, Clifford, Norbert and Patsy. They
also have 11 grandchildren and three great-grandchildren. Noel is married to
Betty Maier and lives in Beulah. They have four children: Jerome, Wayne, John
and Jason.

Clifford is married to Diana Knoell and lives in Beulah. They have two children:
Debbie and Randy. Debbie is married to Faron Scherer and they have a daughter,
Tiffany.

Norbert is married to Marilyn Riedlinger. They also live in Beulah. They have
two children: Jody and David. Jody is married to Lorry Barnick and they have two
daughters: Krista and Erika.

Patsy is married to Mark Frafford and lives on a farm near Halliday. They have
three daughters, Brett, Jessica and Andrea.

Memories of days gone by include the excitement of getting a well next to the
house, eliminating long trips carrying water.

Jack also remembers working with the CCC (Civilian Conservation Corps) in 1934
and 1935 helping build dams and parks in South Dakota near Custer.

The Helm family has enjoyed many outdoor activities, such as boating,
picnicking, and swimming at the lake.

Carl and Marguerite Herman

Carl Herman, son of Charles and Frances (Tavis) Herman, was born July 19, 1904.
He lived with his parents on a sheep ranch south of Beulah from 1904 to 1911,
when the family moved to Center. He attended Center public school, high school
in Glen Ullin, and Capitol Commercial College in Bismarck. He farmed with his
dad until his marriage on Oct. 2, 1933. He and Marguerite McLaughlin were
married by Fr. Bauer at St. Martin's Church at Hazen. Marguerite, the daughter
of Jack and Maggie (Maloney) McLaughlin, was a graduate of Hazen High School
and Dickinson Normal School. She taught school in Hazen, Stanton and Beulah.

        Marguerite and Carl Herman

They moved to a farm south of Beulah, known as the Carl Stephens farm, in 1933
and for four years didn't harvest a bushel of grain. The sand piled up on the
fences and Carl cut Russian thistles for feed for the stock.

On a bright morning in late May, as Marguerite drove to a south school, she
particularly noticed a beautiful 100 acres of wheat standing and on her return
home in the late afternoon, everything was black but the four corners. A strong
north wind had blown the sand over the wheat and the young plants were all cut
off at the roots.

The Hermans were extremely poor but it didn't bother them as all the neighbors
were in the same circumstances. A very bright spot in their lives were the nice
neighbors they had. The neighborhood had dances at the Koesters' home in their
upstairs as it wasn't finished yet. Everyone brought sandwiches or cake and Mrs.
Koester furnished the coffee, dill pickles and her famous ginger snaps.

Every winter there was a Whist Club which met each week and at the close of the
season, the low point players treated the high point players to a home-cooked
supper. Players in the Aplin Whist Club were: Walter Housers, George Clines,
Fred Haucks, August Neubergers, Wilfred Hermans, Carl Hermans, Paul Kosbabs,
Floyd Ericksons, Bill Koesters, Art Stutzs, Ernie Stutzs, Ezra Emigs, Margie
Emig, Freddie Keoster, Shirley Stutz and Willie Houser.

Everyone was interested in the school which also served as a social center for
the community. The Christmas program was the big event of the school year and
everyone came from far and near. There were basket and pie socials to raise
money for library books. Everyone attended the track meets, spelling contests
and declamation matches.

The Herman family always felt they had the best community in North Dakota and
hope that in some small way have helped lay the beginning for the fine schools,
educational system, the lovely churches, the improved methods of farming and the
fine paved roads that cover the trails over which the wagon wheels once rumbled.

Carl and Marguerite were both very interested in school and community affairs.
Carl served on the Greenvale School Board for 18 years and was secretary of the
Mercer County Farmers for 15 years. He was a 4-H Leader, member of the Rural
Fire Department, served on the Aplin Telephone Association, K.C. member and
served as trustee of St. Joseph's Church for many years.

Marguerite has been a member of St. Anne's Altar Society, the Royal Neighbors
for 50 years and is a charter member of the Aplin Homemaker's Club who
celebrated their 40th anniversary in September 1987.

She was chosen Mercer County's Mother of the Year and Beulah Future Homemakers
chapter mother. She was a Farmer's Union youth leader for 14 years, clerk of
Greenvale schools for 15 years, has been secretary of Knife Rivers Farmers
Union for 18 years and is a member of the Beulah TOPS Club.

Carl and Marguerite have four children: Mary Margaret, Marleen, Karen and
Darell. Carl passed away Jan. 28, 1978. Marguerite continues to make her home
on the homeplace south of Beulah.

        Elizabeth, Darell, Mike, Sherty, Sarah Herman

Darell and Sherry Herman

Darell, the son of Carl and Marguerite (McLaughlin) Herman, was born Sept. 16,
1948. He attended grades one through eight at the county school that is located
on the Darell Herman farm. Darell attended Beulah High School, graduating in
1966.

Sherry, the daughter of Elroy and Mabel Herman, was born April 6, 1948. Sherry
attended grades one through twelve at the Beulah Schools, graduating in 1966.
Both attended and graduated from Dickinson State College. Darell received a B.S
degree in business and Sherry received her degree in English. Shortly after
graduation, Darell and Sherry were married at St. Joseph's Catholic Church on
June 12, 1970. Darell's dad soon retired and Darell took over the farm.
Previous to their marriage, Sherry taught high school English in Garrison, where
she also served as head librarian. Following their marriage, Sherry taught
freshman and sophomore English in Hazen for three years.

Darell and Sherry were active members of the Beulah Jaycees and Jayceettes for
several years. During that time, they chaired and worked on numerous projects.
Among them was the Miss Mercer County Pageant, which for three years they
worked in the capacity of producers and director. Darell received several
awards in the Speak Up competitions, and was named Outstanding Jaycee for the
state of North Dakota in 1975. Sherry received awards (Spokette and Sparkette)
for Outstanding Jayceette. Both served as officers and Sherry was president in
1974-1975.

They are members of St. Joseph's Catholic Church and both have served on the
church council. Darell serves on several boards: vice chairman of the Beulah
school board, secretary-treasurer of the Farmer's Union Elevator, director for
the rural electric cooperative and director on the Dickinson State University
board. He is also a member and past officer of the Knights of Columbus,
chairman of the rural firemen and a member of the Beulah Eagles. Sherry has
been a longtime member of the Cheerful Homemakers Club, St. Anne's Altar
Society and Tops 199.

On Jan. 9, 1975, their first daughter, Elizabeth Ann, was born. The following
year on Nov. 10, 1976, a second daughter, Sarah Jane, was added to the family.
The youngest member of the family, Michael James, was born Dec. 14, 1983. Both
Elizabeth and Sarah share interests in band, piano and honor choir and the Knife
River 4-H Club. Elizabeth adds basketball and cheerleading to her list of
activities.

The Hermans reside six miles south and two miles east of Beulah.

Elroy and Mabel Herman

Elroy Herman was born Dec. 9, 1919, in Golden Valley to Emmanuel and Emilia
Herman. He graduated from Beulah High School in 1937. From the summer of '37
until June 1938, Elroy worked for Economy Hardware. In July of 1938, he joined
the CCC's. He was discharged in July 1940. From 1940-41, Elroy worked for Arrow
Creameries. Feb. 17, 1942, Elroy was drafted into the Army where he served
overseas from April 14, 1943 - Nov. 1945.

Upon returning to Beulah, Elroy worked for his father, E.C. Herman, contractor
and builder. Following that, he returned to work for Arrow Creameries. Elroy
married Mabel Pozarnsky of Minot on Oct. 20, 1946. Elroy went to work for MDU in
December 1949. He retired as plant chief Feb. 1, 1984.

Mabel Pozarnsky was born April 14, 1923, to Harry and Anna Pozarnsky at
Benedict. Mabel graduated from McClusky High School and attended Valley City
State College. Before her marriage, Mabel worked as a clerk in the OPA office
and Triple A. Five children were born to this family. Presently, the Hermans
have four surviving children and six grandchildren. One son, Todd, is deceased.

Sherry was born April 6, 1948. She graduated from Beulah High School and
Dickinson State College with a degree in English. She has taught in Garrison and

Helmuth (Doc) and Helen Hilz

        Albert Hoffman family Back: Virgil, Jerome, Nathalja, Dwight, Sylvia,

Albert and Emelia Hoffmann

The Hoffmann history traces back to Adam Hoffmann in the Crimea, Russia. His
son, Joseph Hoffmann, was born in 1851 and married Margaretha Morast. They had a
son, Anton, born Feb. 25, 1878, at Kronental, Crimea, Russia.

On Nov. 3, 1902, Anton married Bertha Murschel. Bertha was born April 28, 1884
to Friedrich and Karolina (Reisz) Murschel.

On Aug. 4, 1903, at Kronental, Crimea, Russia their son Albert was born. On Dec.
17, 1905, Anton and Bertha Hoffmann with their two-year-old son Albert left
Russia for America. They arrived at New York on the ship Rotterdam. Anton
Hoffmann was a farmer in the Crimea, and they homesteaded north of Zap, N.D.

They had two more children, Carolina, born April 10, 1906, who died Feb. 6,
1924, at Zap; and Herbert, born July 25, 1913, who died June 4, 1927, at Zap.

Anton Hoffmann died Aug. 23, 1948, and his wife died Jan. 22. 1959. All are
buried at Zap.

Albert Hoffmann married Emelia Sasse on April 20, 1924. Emelia was born Sept.
23, 1906, at Zap, N.D. to Wilhelm and Theresia (Hinsz) Sasse. Her parents had
come to America in September, 1903 from Alt Elft, Bessarabia, Russia and
homesteaded at Zap. She had four brothers and three sisters. Albert and Emelia
Hoffmann took over his parents' farm in 1927 at Zap, and they continued to farm
until Sept. 4, 1974, when they sold the farm and moved into Beulah, where they
have resided since.

They did move to Dodge in 1945 for four or five years where they had a general
merchandise store. Some of Albert's activities since living in Beulah include
Beulah Special Assessment Board for about 10 years and 12 years on the Germans
from Russia Chapter board of directors. They are members of Zion Lutheran
Church. While living at Zap they were members of Immanuel Lutheran Church, and
Albert took part in many community activities, including the church board,
school board and the FHA board.

They were parents of 12 children, of whom the first eight were born at Zap and
the last four were born at Beulah. They also have 36 grandchildren and one
deceased.

Eleanora Alvina, born September 1924, lives at Grafton State School since age
six.

Viola Lydia, born Dec. 23, 1925, died Feb. 12, 1926, buried at Zap.

Lenhardt Anton, born Jan. 23, 1927, died Nov. 1, 1979, married Carola Benda in
Germany on Sept. 11, 1947. Lived at Toronto, Ontario, Canada.

Raymond Wilhelm, born July 27, 1928, married Martha Funk on Nov. 4, 1953; they
live at Mullin, Idaho.

Mardella Theresia, born Dec. 27, 1929, married Edwin Stuhlmiller on Sept. 14,
1946. They live at Spokane, Wash.

Terry and Mary Lou Horning

Mary Lou Heihn was born April 27, 1948, at St. Alexius Hospital in Bismarck.
She is the daughter of Theodore (Ted) and Martha (Pfenning) Heihn of Beulah.

Mary attended and graduated from Beulah High School in 1966. She was active in
band, choir, FHA and Dial Staff. She went on to attend North Dakota State
University at Fargo and the National College of Business in Rapid City, SD.
After graduating from Business College, Mary was employed by the Federal Civil
Service in Washington, D.C. from 1968-1969. In 1969, she returned to North
Dakota and was employed by the Bismarck Police Department until 1970.

On Aug. 28, 1970, Mary Lou married Terrance Lee (Terry) Horning, son of Emil and
Esther (Morast) Horning of Zap, at the Zion Lutheran Church in Beulah with
Pastor Marvin Schumacher officiating. Terry and Mary moved to Dickinson while
Terry completed college. Mary worked for the Dickinson High School from
1970-1973. After graduation from college in 1972, Terry and Mary moved to
Oregon, where Mary was employed as an auditor for the K-Mart stores in Salem
and Portland, and later worked in the central precinct at the Portland Police
Department.

        Hornings: Justin, Terry, Mary, Brooke, Jason.

In 1974, the Hornings returned to North Dakota and Mary was self-employed as
homemaker and mother until 1986. In 1986, she became a licensed realtor and has
been employed by Century 21 in Beulah since. She was awarded "Top 21" producer
of the state of North Dakota her first year in real estate.

Mary was a past member of the organizing committee and board of directors of the
Little People Preschool from 1978-1986, serving as chairman from 1981-1986; Zion
Lutheran Church Mothers Club; Homemakers; Joachim Memorial Home Board of
Directors, and Zion ALCW. She is presently a member of the Beulah Eagles ladies
Auxiliary, Mercer County Historical Society, Zion Lutheran Church, and the North
Dakota Association of Realtors.

Her husband, Terry attended and graduated from Zap High School in 1965, and
attended Bismarck Junior College in 1966. He enlisted in the U.S. Army during
the Vietnam crisis in 1967. After basic training at Fort Lewis, WA, he was
assigned to Vietnam, serving from 1967-1969. He received an honorable
discharge. In 1972, Terry graduated from Dickinson State College, with a degree
in Business Administration.

While living in Oregon, he was manager for the Meier and Frank Tire Centers in
Portland and Salem. In 1974, after returning to North Dakota, Terry began
employment with Consolidation Coal Company in Stanton, as warehouse supervisor
and later buyer. He worked there from 1975-1985. At present, he is manager of
the Beulah Eagles Club. He is a past member of the VFW, Elks, and Immanual
Lutheran Church of Zap. Presently, Terry is a member of the Beulah Eagles,
Beulah Bowling League, Mercer County Historical Society and he and his family
are members of the Zion Lutheran Church.

Mary and Terry have three children: Jason Matthew, born April 29, 1970, is a
student at Beulah Junior High; Justin Ryan, born Aug. 30, 1978, is a student at
Beulah Elementary School; and Brooke Lindsay, born Aug. 31, 1981, is a student
at Beulah Elementary. Mary and Terry live in Beulah in the house that Ted Heihn
built in 1948 for his family.

Daniel and Katherina Huber as written by Joan Huber

One of 10 children born in Glueckstahl, South Russia, to Jacob and Christina
(nee Voegele) Huber, Daniel was born April 15, 1892. His brothers and sisters
were Jacob, John, Michael, Christina (Mrs. John Bieber), Rosina, Frederick,
Christian, Gottlieb, and David. All are deceased.

The Hubers arrived in America in August 1905 to 1910 (depending on whom you
ask). They settled in the farm area north of Glen Ullin and south of Beulah. The
history of the "New Glueckstahl" Congregational Church, which was organized Nov.
15, 1905, lists Daniel's parents as charter members. Most of these
German-Russian immigrants were sponsored by relatives in America; and thus, the
Hubers homesteaded near other relatives in this North Dakota area.

Daniel did farm labor until he entered the Army in 1917. He was stationed in
Camp Lewis, Wash. His overseas duty during World War I was in France in the
battles of Verdun and Argonne. One out of every 10 soldiers was killed or
wounded in this war; Daniel was among the wounded, with a shell in the leg. In
addition to this, he suffered lung and heart damage as a result of the "gas"
used in the warfare. He was honorably discharged in 1919.

Daniel was one of the 52 original charter members to start a chapter of American
Legion Veterans in Beulah on Oct. 8, 1919. This new organization was
appropriately called "Argonne Post No. 85." (Remember the red poppies and
speeches in the Roxy Theatre?)

Coinciding with the struggles of the Huber family in eking their living from the
drylands and harsh winters in North Dakota, many Russian immigrants joined their
kinsfolk and friends in the "New Glueckstahl" area. Another of these families
was that of Nickolaus and Rosina (nee Veogele) Unruh, who arrived in America
April 12, 1905. In this family, there were 14 children born, but eight had died
by 1905, so six children made the trip to America.

Katherina was the youngest child, born Jan. 30, 1901. Her brothers and sister
were John, Ludwig, Jacob, Christian, and Rosina. Of these Unruhs, Jacob and
Katie are living. Katie helped with the farmwork in her family until her
marriage to Daniel Huber on April 7, 1920.

Hard work and anxious years needed some compensation; and thus a need for
worship was essential. Daniel and Katie were charter members of the Evangelical
Church, started in Beulah March 28, 1921. Katie played the piano, helped in
Sunday school, was active in the Women's Missionary Aid, and fed the ministers
for years. Daniel served on financial boards and attended faithfully until his
death. This church burned to the ground Feb. 13, 1969. (Possibly the Orth home
is now located on this site.)

During their 35 years of marriage, the Hubers built three new homes in Beulah,
which are still existing. They also owned and operated several stores on Main
Street in Beulah, starting their first business about 1925. Daniel built his
last store, the present Sveum's store, in 1947. It was patterned after a market
that son Reinie had seen in Seattle, Wash. An architect drew the plans, the
contractor built those plans, and the building was dedicated Dec. 10, 1947.

It was advertised as "the largest Super Market in Mercer County" at that time.
(Remember the frozen fish outside in a box, the yearly premiums and calendars,
the homemade farmer sausage, the 500 frozen food lockers in the basement, the
new modern grocery carts? Son Leo has an original restored cart and we use it
in our home. And also, do you remember the 12-stool lunch counter with homemade
pastries?)

Daniel was forced to retire from the grocery business due to ill health in 1950
and died Aug. 28, 1955.

Daniel and Katherina were parents of three children - Reinhold J. (deceased in
Lodi, Cal., June 8, 1986), Leo R. (residing in Salt Lake City, Utah), and
Bernice V. (Mrs. Dr. Ted Rath, pastor of the United Methodist Church, Cando,
N.D.) . Reinhold married Jeanette Johnston and they had four sons. Later,
Reinie married Delores Millard and they had three children. Leo married Joan
Baker and they had two daughters; Bernice married Rev. Ted Rath and they had two
sons and two daughters. Thus, Katie, who resides in her own apartment in Cando,
now has 13 grandchildren and 14 great-grandchildren.

With the marriage of Daniel and Katherina (the uniting of the Hubers and the
Unruhs), there were 87 first cousins in the next generation (that is, 48 Huber
cousins and 39 Unruh cousins). Grandfathers Jacob and Nickolaus came to America
to plant new seed, and they were truly able to do this on the fertile soil of
North Dakota. "May the deceased rest from their labors and may their works
follow them."

Jacob and Elizabeth Huber

Jacob Huber was born Dec. 4, 1851 in Heilbrunn, Crimea, Russia to Johann Georg
Huber and a woman whose last name was Mayer.

In July 1874 he left his homeland with other Huber relatives for a new home in
America. They boarded the ship Lessing at Hamburg, Germany on July 23, arriving
in New York on Aug. 5, 1874. They traveled by train to Dakota Territory,
Yankton, S.D., settling in northern Hutchinson County, in the area now near
Freeman, S.D.

Elizabeth Stern was born Sept. 20, 1853 in Kronental, Crimea, Russia to Stephan
and Louisa (Boeshans) Stern. In October 1874, Elizabeth, her parents, six
brothers and two sisters arrived in Dakota Territory. They settled in the Wolf
Creek area near Freeman, S.D.

Jacob and Elizabeth (Stern) Huber were married in 1875 and had 14 children while
homesteading in South Dakota. Six sons and one daughter died as infants, most of
high fever which could have been either scarlet fever or diphtheria. They are
buried in unmarked graves by their grandparents, the Sterns. All were born and
died before 1899.

In 1898 Jacob Huber, Fred Mettler, Sr. and Jacob Hafner came to North Dakota
looking for land. At this time Jacob Huber had three sons ready to farm. Land
was all taken in their area and if the land was for sale it was expensive. Late
in March, 1899, the Hubers, Hafners, Mettlers, Schramms, Bohrers, Mastels and
Wiederichs, with their families, all came by passenger train from Tripp, S.D.
to New Salem, N.D. They all settled in Mercer County. The Huber family settled
north of Beulah.

Jacob Stephen Huber, always known as "Steve," was born May 17, 1876; died May
31, 1914, and is buried unmarked in St. John's Lutheran cemetery at Krem, N.D.
Steve Huber was married Aug. 27, 1895 in Hutchinson County, S.D. to Elizabeth
Wiedenmeyer who was born in 1877 to Edward and Barbara (Bub) Wiedenmeyer.
Elizabeth died in 1906 in childbirth, along with her baby, and is also buried
in Krem in an unmarked grave.

Their children were:

Emma, born June 4, 1896 in South Dakota, died Sept. 29, 1965 was married to Nels
Anderson and lived at Baldwin, N.D.

Odelia "Tillie," born 1902 in Mercer County, died in 1952 in Miles City, Mont.
She was married to Alec Braun and lived in Terry, Mont. Tillie remarried to
Bill Remmick and lived at Wolf Point, Mont. Tillie is buried at Terry, Mont.

Reinhold was born June 27, 1905 in Mercer County, died Feb. 19, 1967, was
married to Emma Rupp, both buried at Baldwin, N.D.

Steve Huber remarried to a niece of his first wife, Pauline Wiedenmeyer, a
daughter of Joe Wiedenmeyer, who was born April 19, 1885, died April 1, 1908 and
is buried at St. John's Lutheran Cemetery at Krem.

Ted, born March 22, 1907 in Mercer County, married Margaret Mock and had 11
children. Ted lives near Crane, Mont.

Jacob and Elizabeth's second child, Mattias "Matt," was born Sept. 2, 1878, died
March 27, 1911 and is buried north of Beulah at Peace Lutheran Cemetery. Matt
married Rosina Richau on Feb. 12, 1905. She was born April 4, 1884 to Komelius
and Katharina (Goetz) Richau. Rosina remarried to John Renner and died Oct. 12,
1962. Both are buried at Trinity Lutheran Cemetery at Kronthal.

Of Matt's children, Gideon was born Feb. 14, 1907 in the Kasmer community,
worked for many years for the Hafner families. Gideon never married and died
April 20, 1969. He is buried at Trinity Lutheran Cemetery at Kronthal.

Leo was born Nov. 27, 1908 in the Kasmer community. Leo is still on his father's
homestead. Leo married Edna Renner on Sept. 8, 1932 and had four children:
Lorretta, Marlene, (Mrs. Robert Schreifer at Golden Valley, N.D.) Frances and
Clarence at Hazen, N.D.

Carolina was born Nov. 17, 1909, in the Kasmer community, died Nov. 18, 1909
and is buried on the Matt Huber homestead, grave unmarked.

Melita was born July 26, 1910 in the Kasmer community, died Oct. 12, 1910 and is
buried at Peace Lutheran Cemetery north of Beulah. Grave is unmarked.

Jacob and Elizabeth's third child, Michael, was born Jan. 4, 1880, homesteaded
in Mercer County. He married Emma Thomas and had four children before leaving by
covered wagon in 1915, traveling to South Dakota to visit friends and relatives
and settling in northern Colorado. Michael died in 1942 and is buried in
Colorado. Emma (Thomas) Huber was born May 21, 1877, died Nov. 26, 1958 at
Brush, Colo. and is buried at Fort Morgan, Colo.

Of their four children, Walter was born Jan. 16, 1909, and lives in a rest home
in Colorado. Alive 1982, never married.

Lena was born Dec. 21, 1911, alive in 1982 in Colorado, married a Tehonovich.

Amanda was born March 24, 1913, alive in 1982 in Colorado, married a Krook.

Alma was born March 24, 1913, died in 1977, was married to a Klem.

Gottlieb Kruckenberg, Jr. on Dec. 5, 1901 at Expansion, N.D. by Rev. Engelder.
Lived all her married life seven miles north of Zap. Louisa died at her home at
the young age of 43 years from cancer on Jan. 25, 1928. Gottlieb Kruckenberg
was born at Benkendorf, Bessarabia, Russia to Gottlieb and Dorothea (Habelmann)
Kruckenberg on July 22, 1880. The Kruckenberg family came to Dakota Territory,
settling at Expansion, N.D. in December 1888. Gottlieb died Jan. 13, 1944. Both

They were the parents of 17 children:

Jacob and Elizabeth's fifth child, John, was born May 3, 1885, and homesteaded
north of Beulah. Leon Walz is now on that homestead. John died March 14, 1953

Knittel on Nov. 5, 1907. Emelia was born Feb. 23, 1890 at Freeman, S.D. to Jacob

They were the parents of five children.

To do this history I've done personal visits to Freeman and Menno, S D., all
over Mercer County N.D., Crane and Terry, Mont. History compiled by great-
granddaughter Mrs. Viola "Vi" (Kruckenberg) Schielke, Beulah.

Leo and Joan Huber

As you may (or may not) know, the Bible goes on for pages, chapters, and books
from Genesis through Acts, telling of the "begats" of all generations from Adam
to Jesus Christ.

Eighteen hundred years later, these are the generations of the Huber family as
recorded by our forefathers:

Jacob Huber (born 1851, died 1933) begat Daniel Huber (born April 15, 1892, died
Aug. 28, 1955); Daniel begat Leo Reuben Huber (born Nov. 30, 1927, living) .
Nickolaus Unruh (born March 7, 1860, died April 6, 1939) begat Katherina (Unruh)
Huber (born Jan. 30, 1901, living); Katherina begat (or was begatting done by
males only?) Leo Reuben Huber.

Now, these are the generations of the Baker family: George Baker (born 1852,
died Feb. 13, 1935) and Mary Elizabeth Giles Baker (born 1862, died June 29,
1933) begat Henry John Baker (born March 10, 1894, died April 5, 1963); Henry
begat Joan (Baker) Huber (born Jan. 16, 1929, living).

Gilbert B. Beck (born Oct. 10, 1854, died Jan. 15, 1938) and Sarah Victoria
Young Beck (born Sept. 16, 1866, died Nov. 13, 1912) begat Myrtle Blanche Beck
(born Jan. 15, 1892, died June 30, 1985); Myrtle begat Joan (Baker) Huber.

As a "begotten," Leo was born on Nov. 30, 1927, in Beulah to Daniel and
Katherina (nee Unruh) Huber. He grew up in the grocery store atmosphere, where
he watched his father butcher the animals and process the meat to sell in the
store. He "candled" eggs over a metal can that had an electric bulb in it at
the age of six. Attending grade school and high school at the Beulah School, he
graduated in 1945. He didn't go on to college due to his father's poor health,
but instead started managing Huber's Food Market at 17. He was interested in
all sports and played basketball and football four years in high school and
later refereed the Beulah High School games.

Leo had no military training, but had his physical at Fort Snelling, Minn.,
when World War II ended.

In another little hamlet in North Dakota--namely, Fingal--Joan Baker was born
Jan. 16, 1929, to Henry John Baker and Myrtle Blanche (Beck) Baker. Baker
barbered in Fingal for 10 years. In 1931, he sought employment in Beulah and so
the family of five moved. Joan also attended Beulah High School for all 12
years and graduated in 1947. Her interests in school were singing, tap dancing,
and drama. (Remember the Christmas programs in the Roxy Theater? Joan was Mary,
Mother of Jesus, several years - always singing a solo.) Joan did not go on to
further education, but found the necessity of working a priority at that time.

Her religious faith was in the Congregational Church as a child. Later, at age
18, she was baptized, confirmed, and became a member of the Evangelical United
Brethren church in Beulah.

At age 12, she started her first job as a telephone operator for Kathleen
Erdman at $1 a day, placing long distance calls to New York, California, and
Florida. As a teenager, Joan was a "soda jerk" in the Beulah Drug Store.
(Remember "muds" and cherry or lime cokes?) Eventually, Joan was hired as a
clerk in Huber's Food Market. And, yes, you guessed it, she and Leo started
dating.

They were married July 18, 1948, in the Evangelical United Brethren Church with
Rev. Solomon S. Gruneich officiating.

Joan worked as a teller and bookkeeper in the Bank of Beulah from 1949-1951. Leo
continued managing his father's store.

More begatting! Leo and Joan begat Darsha Lee (Sept. 15, 1951) and Karma Ree
(Aug. 29, 1954). Darsha married Carl Hultgren and they begat two children
(Sherri Lee and Mark David) . Karma married Gerhard Bombe and they have no
begottens.

In 1952, the Hubers sold the business and leased the building to Hanewald and
Weigum of Hazen; George Bentz managed for them. Leo then worked as a clerk for
Bill Unruh at Beulah Hardware for one year. In 1953 and 1954, Leo worked for
Liebelt Chevrolet, selling cars and quonset buildings. In 1955 and part of
1956, Leo and J.B. Field went into partnership, selling Dodge and Plymouth
cars. This business was dissolved in the spring of 1956, when Leo and Joan moved
to southern California.

Leo started as a clerk with the A & P Markets in Torrance, Calif., on the third
day in California. Eighteen months later, Fox Markets offered him a better
position. Leo worked for them until he joined the Food Giant Markets. In 1970,
Smith's Food King of Salt Lake City bought all the Food Giants. Leo has been
with them since that time. He managed several stores in the Los Angeles area,
including Beverly Hills. He progressed from clerk to assistant manager to store
director to personnel director of the California-Nevada division to safety
director of the Smith's Management Corporation, which is his present position.
The sale of the California division (34 stores) in 1984 and Leo's promotion to
the corporate office were the incentives to move to Salt Lake City, where they
now reside.

Leo's responsibilities include supervising eight states with approximately 100
stores, plus warehouses, bakery, dairy, etc. His work involves  inspections,
training, reports, lawsuits, reports, and reports! His goals are to retire in
five years and perhaps move back to southern California.

Joan has had a variety of interests and achievements through the years.
Attending a tea and luncheon for - and talking with --First Lady Pat Nixon;
singing in the Billy Graham Crusade for nine nights; teaching Sunday school 25
consecutive years; holding the flaming torch during the Torch Run in 1984;
singing in a church choir 25 years; attending five events during the Olympic
Games in Los Angeles in 1984; singing in a mass choir of 250 in the Symphony
Hall in Salt Lake City; singing each week in the choir of the First United
Methodist Church downtown; delivering "Meals on Wheels" weekly for six years,
each week; and many hours of volunteer work for the elderly. All this is
probably not recorded anywhere but in Joan's heart and memories.

Their first begotten, Darsha, is a secretary for the Xerox Corporation in El
Segundo, Calif. Her first begotten, Sherri Lee, is a sophomore at Pepperdine
University in Malibu, Calif. Darsha's other begotten, Mark David, is a
sophomore at Torrance High School and very interested in volleyball.

Leo and pan's second begotten, Karma, is a display supervisor for "The Nature
Company" and does displays from Beverly Hills to San Diego, Calif. Her husband,
Gerhard, is a landscape architect for Orange County, Calif., and designs parks
for the parks and recreation department. They live in a condo in San Clemente.

And these are the generations of the Hubers and the Bakers.

        Hubers: Janella, Ella, Melwon, Melvia

Melwon H. and Ella Huber

Melwon Huber was born Jan. 22, 1922, in Oliver County, to Albert and Henrietta
(Guenthner) Huber. Melwon married Ella Weil who was born July 6, 1922, in Mercer
County to August and Mary (Fey) Weil of Beulah. Melwon is retired now but did
work seven and a half years for Knife River Coal Co. and 32 years for Farmers
Union Oil Co.

They are parents of two daughters: Melvia, born Oct. 1, 1947, at Beulah,
married to Don Renner and lives at Beulah; Janella, born June 13, 1953, at
Hazen Hospital, married to Jim Hausauer and lives at Halliday, N.D.

The Hubers are active members of Concordia Lutheran Church and the Beulah
Senior Citizens. Melwon has served as a board member of the Joachim Memorial
Home, Concordia Lutheran Church, Beulah Nursing Home and Beulah Senior Citizens.

        Chris M. and Alida Iverson

Chris M. and Alida Iverson

Chris M. Iverson was born on July 11, 1880, at Browntown, WI. Alida (Helland)
Iverson was born on Sept. 19, 1887, at Bergan, Norway. She came to the United
States and settled with relatives in Browntown, WI, where she met and married
Chris in 1911. That same year they came to North Dakota and homesteaded on 80
acres in Mercer county. They knew that this was not enough land to make a
living so they bought additional land. This land is now part of the Galster
Farm north of Beulah.

They left Wisconsin on a Monday with a carload of machinery, horses and
household goods and arrived in Glen Ullin on Friday. When they were going from
Glen Ullin to the homestead they stopped at the George Weigum farm. George
thought they were going to steal some grain. This confusion came about because
there was a language barrier between them. Chris couldn't speak German and
George couldn't speak English, so George sent one of his boys to the Eugene
Foster farm to get help. Foster knew Chris since they had gotten acquainted the
year before when Chris came to North Dakota looking for land, and took the new
settlers home with him to spend the night at the Foster Place, after assuring
George that his wheat was safe.

Because Chris was very concerned about his children's education and wanted to
live closer to school, they sold the homestead and bought another farm on the
north edge of Beulah, or what is now known as the Gateway Addition. This farm
was sold to the Wilfert family in 1941.

From 1918-1922 Chris was the Star Route mail carrier and transported many
passengers and much freight to the stores at Ree. In 1922 he was appointed mail
carrier for the rural route north of Beulah, where he worked until he retired
in 1950.

Mr. Iverson operated a livery stable on the lots where the Thomas Body Shop is
now located. In fact at one time he owned that entire block. He was also the
first Standard Oil Bulk Agent in Beulah.

Alida passed away in 1935 and for the next two years Chris rented out his farm
and moved into town. He married Mattie Caldwell and moved back to the farm.

The Iversons had six children - four of whom are deceased: Ivan, 1914-1932;
Vida, 1916-1938; Melvin, 1918-1919; and Norman, 1920-1977. Annabelle, (Mrs. Bob
Easton) lives in Bismarck; and Lloyd, who lives in Milwaukee, WI. The Iverson
children attended and graduated from Beulah High School with the exception of
Annabelle who graduated from Dickinson Model High School.

The Iverson family attended the Beulah Congregational Church until an English
Lutheran Congregation was organized, which they joined. Later this congregation
became part of Zion Lutheran Church. The Iverson family was always very active
in church affairs. Alida was an active member of the Mission Circle and Cris,
Vida, and Norman sang in the church choir. Norman, Vida, and Annabelle taught
Sunday School. Annabelle was a member of Mission Circle and the ALCW for 32
years and taught Sunday school for 33 years.

Chris retired in 1950 and he and Mattie moved to Longwiew, WA. Chris passed away
in 1968 and Mattie in 1973.

Jerald and Marilyn Iverson

Jerald Iverson was born May 10, 1940, in Dupree, S.D., and presently works for
the Montana-Dakota Utilities Company as the safety training coordinator. His
father Tilvert passed away Nov. 2, 1976, and his mother Stella is still living.
His wife Marilyn (Quenzer) was born Feb. 22, 1944, in Mobridge, S.D. Her father
Ervin lives in Mobridge, and her mother Estelline passed away May 24, 1986.

They have three children: Thomas, born April 14, 1966; Patrice, born June 20,
1967; and Elizabeth, born July 11, 1968. All the children were born in Mobridge.

The family hold membership with Immanuel Baptist Church, where they have worked
in the Awana Clubs and other church organizations. Jerry is also a member of
the Spring Creek Horseshoe Club and bowls for the Security State Bank.

The Iverson family came to Beulah in December 1979, when the Coyote station
began operating. They moved here from Sidney, Mont., and prior to that lived at
Mobridge for 13 years. All of the family has enjoyed living in Beulah and all
three of the children have graduated from high school here. Patty has recently
been a waitress at Dakota Farms Cafe, while Libby has been employed at the
Beulah nursing home as a dietary aide.

        Christ Jacober family

and his mother Kate (Kemmet) passed away Aug. 30, 1964. Christ married Martha

Clarence and Leah Jaeger

Clarence Jaeger was born Oct. 22, 1933 in Beulah, to August and Rose Jaeger. He
grew up in the Beulah-Zap area and graduated from Beulah High School. After
serving two years in the US. Army, he returned to Beulah and went into the

In 1962, Clarence married Leah Lackman, daughter of Alex and Marie Lackman of
